title: Main Computer
description: Physical capacity for development, local testing, and a small infrastructure lab.

items.name: Main workstation
items.detail: Laptop or desktop that can comfortably run VS Code, browsers, Git, Node.js, and documentation tools.

items.name: Memory
items.detail: 16 GB is a workable minimum; 32 GB or more is preferred for multiple Windows and Linux virtual machines.

items.name: Storage
items.detail: At least 250 GB free for repositories, ISO files, VM disks, screenshots, and exported lab backups.

items.name: External SSD
items.detail: Useful for VM storage, lab backups, and moving lab assets between machines.

title: Virtualisation
description: The lab needs a safe place to create and destroy servers, clients, and test networks.

items.name: Hyper-V
items.detail: Good first choice on Windows for DC01, APP01, Windows clients, and Linux VMs.

items.name: Proxmox
items.detail: Strong later option for a dedicated homelab host and more realistic infrastructure practice.

items.name: Snapshots
items.detail: Use snapshots before major changes so you can recover from broken services, GPO mistakes, and failed installs.

items.name: Isolated lab network
items.detail: Keep lab domain services separate from your normal home network unless you know exactly what is being exposed.

title: Software
description: Core tools used to build the website, document the lab, and automate infrastructure tasks.

items.name: VS Code
items.detail: Primary editor for HTML, CSS, JavaScript, JSON, Markdown, PowerShell, Python, Terraform, and YAML.

items.name: Node.js
items.detail: Required for Vite, local development, production builds, and future frontend tooling.

items.name: Git
items.detail: Version control system used to save progress, compare changes, and build a portfolio history.

items.name: Git Bash
items.detail: Preferred command-line environment for Git commands and consistent project workflow on Windows.

items.name: PowerShell 7
items.detail: Modern PowerShell runtime for automation scripts, modules, API calls, and cross-platform scripting.

items.name: Windows Admin Center
items.detail: Useful later for Windows Server administration and hybrid management practice.

title: Accounts and Subscriptions
description: External services needed for source control, Microsoft learning, cloud identity, and deployment.

items.name: GitHub account
items.detail: Hosts the repository, commit history, documentation, issues, releases, GitHub Pages, and Actions workflows.

items.name: Microsoft Learn account
items.detail: Tracks learning progress across Windows Server, Azure, Entra ID, Intune, and PowerShell content.

items.name: Microsoft 365 developer tenant
items.detail: Useful for Entra ID, Intune, Graph API, app registrations, users, groups, and policy testing.

items.name: Azure subscription
items.detail: Optional early on, useful later for AZ-104, Terraform provider practice, and cloud infrastructure labs.

items.name: Docker Hub or container registry
items.detail: Useful later for image publishing and container deployment workflows.

title: Licences
description: Software licensing to plan for before the lab grows into Microsoft 365, Intune, or Windows Server work.

items.name: Windows evaluation media
items.detail: Use official evaluation images for Windows Server and Windows client lab machines where appropriate.

items.name: Microsoft 365 test licensing
items.detail: Needed for serious Entra ID, Intune, Conditional Access, Autopilot, and endpoint management testing.

items.name: Open source tools
items.detail: Linux, Docker, Terraform, Ansible, Prometheus, Grafana, and many lab tools can be learned with free tooling.

title: Networking
description: Basic network design is required before domain services, Linux services, Docker, and Kubernetes make sense.

items.name: IP addressing plan
items.detail: Document lab subnets, static server IPs, DHCP ranges, gateway addresses, and reserved addresses.

items.name: DNS plan
items.detail: Document internal domain names, A records, CNAMEs, forwarders, and reverse lookup requirements.

items.name: DHCP scope design
items.detail: Define address pools, reservations, lease duration, DNS options, and test renewal commands.

items.name: Firewall rules
items.detail: Track what ports are required for AD, DNS, DHCP, SSH, HTTP, HTTPS, WinRM, and monitoring.

items.name: Troubleshooting commands
items.detail: Practise ipconfig, ping, nslookup, Resolve-DnsName, Test-NetConnection, traceroute, ss, and journalctl.

title: Documentation
description: The portfolio value comes from proving what was built, what broke, and how it was fixed.

items.name: README
items.detail: Explain the project purpose, setup steps, folder structure, local run commands, and deployment URL.

items.name: Architecture diagrams
items.detail: Create simple diagrams for the lab network, domain, automation flow, and deployment flow.

items.name: Troubleshooting notes
items.detail: Record errors, symptoms, commands used, root cause, fix, and prevention notes.

items.name: Screenshots
items.detail: Capture important proof points such as domain joins, GPO results, script output, dashboards, and deployments.

items.name: Runbooks
items.detail: Write repeatable steps for onboarding, leavers, service recovery, deployment, backup, and restore.

title: Lab Equipment
description: Ideal for expanding the lab into a more realistic infrastructure environment with multiple servers, clients, and network segments.

items.name: Dedicated mini PC
items.detail: Can run Proxmox, multiple VMs, Docker stacks, monitoring, and longer-running infrastructure experiments.

items.name: Managed switch
items.detail: Useful later for VLANs, network segmentation, and more realistic infrastructure practice.

items.name: NAS or backup disk
items.detail: Useful for VM backups, ISO storage, exported reports, screenshots, and recovery testing.

items.name: Test PCs
items.detail: Useful later for Autopilot, Intune enrollment, endpoint compliance, and real device troubleshooting.
